evidence_quote: ## Content Search Informing humanitarians worldwide 24/7 — a service provided by UN OCHA [DR Congo](/country/cod) + 14 more # Multi-country outbreak of mpox, External situation report #42 - 9 November 2024 Format : Situation Report Source : * [WHO](/organization/who) Posted Originally published Origin : [View original](https://www.who.int/publications/m/item/multi-country-outbreak-of-mpox--external-situation-report--42--9-november-2024) ## Attachments * [![Preview of 20241109_mpox_external-sitrep_-42.pdf](/sites/default/files/styles/small/public/previews/f6/23/f6238fd2-5642-432e-a66f-09905adce059.png?2584935-1-0) **Download Report** (PDF | 1.2 MB)](/attachments/f6238fd2-5642-432e-a66f-09905adce059/20241109_mpox_external-sitrep_-42.pdf) **Highlights** • Since the last situation report, three additional countries have confirmed travel-related cases of clade Ib MPXV: the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland, Zambia and Zimbabwe. • For the first time, local transmission of clade Ib MPXV was reported outside of Africa, in the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland, where three (all) household members of the initial case (who had travelled to affected East African countries with clade Ib) were confirmed to have mpox. • The number of mpox cases in Africa shows a general rising trend, driven mainly by cases reported from the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Burundi, and Uganda. • As of 3 November 2024, Clade Ib monkeypox virus (MPXV) has been detected in six provinces in the Democratic Republic of the Congo: South Kivu, North Kivu, Kinshasa, Kasai, Tshopo and Tanganyika, with no new areas known to be affected since the last update. Additionally, 11 other countries have also reported clade Ib MPXV cases.

Share sensitive information only on official, secure websites. ![CDC Logo](/TemplatePackage/4.0/assets/imgs/logo/logo-notext.svg) ![CDC Logo](/TemplatePackage/4.0/assets/imgs/logo/logo-notext.svg) # Monkeypox Caused by Human-to-Human Transmission of *Monkeypox Virus* in the Democratic Republic of the Congo with Spread to Neighboring Countries ![Health Alert Network logo.](/han/images/HAN-Logo240x116px.png?_=71758) ![HAN_badge_HEALTH_UPDATE_320x125](/han/images/HAN_badge_HEALTH_UPDATE_320x125.png?_=71757 "HAN_badge_HEALTH_UPDATE_320x125.png") Distributed via the CDC Health Alert Network August 7, 2024, 3:15 PM ET CDCHAN-00513 **Summary** The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) is issuing this Health Alert Network (HAN) Health Update to provide additional information about the outbreak of monkeypox virus (MPXV) in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC); the first [Health Advisory](https://emergency.cdc.gov/han/2023/han00501.asp) about this outbreak was released in December 2023. Since January 2023, the DRC has reported the largest number of yearly suspected clade I monkeypox cases on record. While clade I MPXV is endemic, or naturally occurring, in DRC, the current outbreak is more widespread than any previous DRC outbreak and has resulted in clade I monkeypox transmission to some neighboring countries.
